name: Martin Luther

born.place: Eisleben, County of Mansfeld, Holy Roman Empire (now Saxony-Anhalt, Germany)

died.place: Eisleben, County of Mansfeld, Holy Roman Empire (now Saxony-Anhalt, Germany)

life_summary: Martin Luther was born in Eisleben on 10 November 1483. This is the traditional date, and the Neue Deutsche Biographie marks it as uncertain. In 1484 the family moved to Mansfeld, where his father worked in copper mining. After arts studies at Erfurt he entered the Augustinian friary there in July 1505 and was ordained priest in 1507. From 1511 he lived in Wittenberg, where he became doctor of theology in 1512 and was preaching at the town church from 1514. His 95 Theses on indulgences of 31 October 1517 started a dispute that led to his excommunication in January 1521 and to his refusal to recant before the Diet of Worms that April. Placed under the imperial ban, he was hidden at the Wartburg until March 1522 and translated the New Testament into German there. Back in Wittenberg he led the reform of worship and church life. He married the former nun Katharina von Bora in 1525, and they had six children, two of whom died young. He published the complete German Bible in 1534 and wrote catechisms and many polemical works, including a hostile 1543 tract against the Jews. Illness troubled him more and more in these years. He died in Eisleben on 18 February 1546 and was buried in Wittenberg's Castle Church.

phases.label: Childhood and Erfurt studies
phases.summary: Born in Eisleben and raised in Mansfeld, he went to school in Mansfeld, Magdeburg (from 1497) and Eisenach (from 1498). From 1501 he studied arts at Erfurt and took his bachelor's degree in September 1502 and his master's degree (December 1504 according to NDB, 1505 in other accounts), then began law studies in the summer semester of 1505.

sources.label: Gerhard Müller, 'Luther, Martin', Neue Deutsche Biographie 15 (1987)

phases.label: Augustinian friar at Erfurt
phases.summary: He entered the Augustinian friary at Erfurt in July 1505, took vows in 1506, was ordained priest in 1507 and studied theology, including a teaching spell at Wittenberg from autumn 1508 into 1509. He travelled to Rome on business for his order: NDB dates the journey to about November 1510 to early 1511, while Kohnle gives 1511/12.

sources.label: Gerhard Müller, 'Luther, Martin', Neue Deutsche Biographie 15 (1987)

phases.label: Wittenberg professor and preacher
phases.summary: His order moved him to Wittenberg in September 1511. He was elected subprior of the Augustinian house in 1512, received his doctorate that October and lectured on the Psalms, Romans and Galatians. He preached at the town church from 1514 and was elected district vicar of his order in 1515.

sources.label: Gerhard Müller, 'Luther, Martin', Neue Deutsche Biographie 15 (1987)

phases.label: Indulgence controversy to Worms
phases.summary: His theses on indulgences led to the Heidelberg Disputation (April 1518), a hearing before Cardinal Cajetan in Augsburg, the Leipzig Debate with Johann Eck and his major treatises of 1520. He was excommunicated in January 1521, refused to recant at the Diet of Worms in April 1521 and was then placed under the imperial ban.

sources.label: Gerhard Müller, 'Luther, Martin', Neue Deutsche Biographie 15 (1987)

phases.label: Wartburg exile
phases.summary: From May 1521 he lived hidden at the Wartburg near Eisenach as 'Junker Jörg', under the protection of Elector Frederick. There he wrote a postil of model sermons for preachers and translated the New Testament into German. He paid a secret visit to Wittenberg in December 1521 and left the Wartburg for good on 1 March 1522.

sources.label: Gerhard Müller, 'Luther, Martin', Neue Deutsche Biographie 15 (1987)

phases.label: Wittenberg reform and marriage
phases.summary: Back in Wittenberg he preached, lectured and advised on church reform. In the 1525 Peasants' War he first urged peace and then called on rulers to put down the revolt. He married Katharina von Bora in June 1525; three children were born between 1526 and 1529, and one of them, Elisabeth, died in 1528. He stayed in the town during the 1527 plague, wrote his catechisms in 1529 and met Zwingli at Marburg that October.

sources.label: Gerhard Müller, 'Luther, Martin', Neue Deutsche Biographie 15 (1987)
Christopher Gehrz, 'Courage and pestilence', Christian History 135 (2020)

phases.label: Later Wittenberg years
phases.summary: From April to October 1530 he stayed at Coburg Castle during the Diet of Augsburg, and there he learned of his father's death. His mother died in 1531. Back in Wittenberg he taught, preached and wrote, and he completed the German Bible in 1534. Kidney stones and other illnesses troubled him more and more, and his daughter Magdalena died in 1542. He lectured until 17 November 1545 and preached in Halle and Eisleben on his last journey, which ended with his death in Eisleben in February 1546.

sources.label: Gerhard Müller, 'Luther, Martin', Neue Deutsche Biographie 15 (1987)

events.event: Born in Eisleben to Hans Luder and Margarethe Lindemann. NDB marks the date as uncertain. The family moved to nearby Mansfeld in 1484.
According to his own later account, he vowed to become a monk when he was caught in a thunderstorm near Stotternheim on his way back to Erfurt.
Entered the Augustinian friary in Erfurt and gave up the law studies his father wanted for him.
Ordained priest; he celebrated his first Mass on 2 May 1507.
Received his doctorate in theology at Wittenberg and took over Johann von Staupitz's professorship of biblical exegesis.
Began preaching regularly at Wittenberg's town church alongside his university lectures.
Sent his 95 Theses on indulgences to Archbishop Albrecht of Mainz and the Bishop of Brandenburg. Scholars disagree on whether he also posted them on the Castle Church door.
Questioned by Cardinal Cajetan at Augsburg, he refused to recant. He left the city secretly on 20 October and was back in Wittenberg on 31 October.
Debated Johann Eck at Leipzig, where he questioned papal primacy and admitted that church councils could err.
Outside Wittenberg's Elster Gate he burned the papal bull threatening him with excommunication, along with books of canon law. The excommunication was confirmed on 3 January 1521.
Appeared before Emperor Charles V at the Diet of Worms and refused to recant his writings unless refuted by Scripture or clear reason.
On his way home from Worms he was seized near Altenstein in a staged ambush arranged by the Saxon court and hidden at the Wartburg.
Back in Wittenberg since 6 March, he began a series of daily sermons in the town church on Invocavit Sunday.
His German New Testament, translated at the Wartburg in about eleven weeks, was published as the 'September Testament'.
During the Peasants' War he wrote a tract calling on rulers to put down the rebel peasants by force, which drew lasting criticism.
Married Katharina von Bora, a former nun. After the wedding the couple lived in Wittenberg's former Augustinian friary, the Black Cloister.

sources.label: luther.de: Marriage to Katharina von Bora

events.event: His first child, Hans (Johannes), was born. Five more children followed by December 1534.

sources.label: Augenblick mal! (kip-nrw / pep.ekir): Die Kinder von Martin Luther
St. John's Lutheran Church: A Brief History of the Luther Children

events.event: Plague reached Wittenberg. Luther stayed in the town to minister to the sick and that year wrote 'Whether One May Flee from a Deadly Plague'.

sources.label: Christopher Gehrz, 'Courage and pestilence', Christian History 135

events.event: Met Ulrich Zwingli at the Marburg Colloquy. They failed to agree on Christ's presence in the Lord's Supper.
His father died while Luther was staying at Coburg Castle during the Diet of Augsburg. A letter brought him the news on 5 June.

sources.label: German History in Documents and Images: Luther and his Father (June 5, 1530)

events.event: The first complete edition of his German translation of the whole Bible was published.
Wrote the Smalcald Articles as his theological testament. At the Schmalkalden meeting that year a severe kidney-stone attack made him believe he was dying, as he wrote to Katharina.
His daughter Magdalena died at the age of 13 after an illness.

sources.label: Augenblick mal! (kip-nrw / pep.ekir): Die Kinder von Martin Luther
luther.de: Luther's Death and Last Years

events.event: Published 'On the Jews and Their Lies', a hostile polemic that departed sharply from his conciliatory 1523 tract 'That Jesus Christ Was Born a Jew'.

sources.label: luther.de: Luther's Death and Last Years

events.event: Died in Eisleben after mediating a dispute among the Mansfeld counts. He was buried in Wittenberg's Castle Church on 22 February, where Bugenhagen preached the funeral sermon.

sources.label: Gerhard Müller, 'Luther, Martin', Neue Deutsche Biographie 15 (1987), Deutsche Biographie

Eric W. Gritsch, 'Unstoppable' (Luther's illnesses), Christian History 39 (1993)
